land.text: the northern San Juan outliers around Aztec Ruins on the Animas River, which Cliopatria carries on as a separate regional system from 1152

successors.note: The page (Chaco Culture NHP) says Salmon and Aztec Ruins 'were built during a thirty-year wet period commencing in 1100' as north outliers; the rest of the Chaco land was abandoned (see the dissolve event).

capitals.name: Chaco Canyon (Pueblo Bonito)
capitals.note: The pages name a 'major cultural center' (900-1150) with Pueblo Bonito the richest burial site, not a capital; the dot marks the centre of the system.

keyframe_review.note: 850-1039, 21,200 km2 around Chaco Canyon. The page: 'By 850, the Ancient Pueblo population had rapidly expanded' and 'Between 900 and 1150, Chaco Canyon was a major cultural center'; Una Vida 'construction began around 900'. No page gives an extent for these years, so the shape stands unverified in size; the infobox gives no area.

1040-1146, 64,974 km2. The page gives the San Juan Basin as 25,000 sq mi (65,000 km2), which this shape matches, and 'Thirty such outliers spread across 65,000 sq mi (170,000 km2)' (ratio 0.38; the larger figure is the spread of the outliers' scatter, not a territory, so the shape is kept). 'By AD 1115 at least 70 outlying pueblos of Chacoan provenance had been built'; building boom 1020-1050, most beams cut 1033-1092. The page does not date the spread of the outlier network to 1040.

1147-1151, same 64,974 km2. 'The cohesive Chacoan system began to unravel around 1140' and 'Outlying communities began to depopulate' after a drought 'that began in 1130', but the page names no region that emptied first, so the shape is not contracted; the page's end for the canyon centre is 1150 ('Between 900 and 1150'), one year before Cliopatria's 1151.

region.text: Chaco Canyon and the surrounding San Juan Basin, where 'the Ancient Pueblo population had rapidly expanded'

ledger.note: 850: the Ancestral Puebloan population of Chaco Canyon has 'rapidly expanded'. The page's wording is 'By 850, the Ancient Pueblo population had rapidly expanded'; it calls Chaco a 'major cultural center' only from 900 ('Between 900 and 1150'), and Una Vida began about 900. The start year and the region are Cliopatria's (21,203 km2).

region.text: the wider San Juan Basin and its outlying great houses and roads, 25,000 sq mi (65,000 km2)

ledger.note: 1040: the Chacoan system spreads over the San Juan Basin. The page is silent on the year the outlier network formed: it dates a building boom ('Pueblo Alto ... begun between AD 1020 and 1050'; 'Most of the beams used at Chaco were cut between 1033 and 1092'), 'By AD 1115 at least 70 outlying pueblos of Chacoan provenance had been built' and Salmon and Aztec Ruins to 'a thirty-year wet period commencing in 1100'. The 1040 date and the extent are Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Chacoan land of the San Juan Basin

ledger.note: 1151: the Chacoan system is gone. 'Between 900 and 1150, Chaco Canyon was a major cultural center'; 'The cohesive Chacoan system began to unravel around 1140' after 'an extreme 50-year drought that began in 1130'; 'by the end of the century the buildings in the central canyon had been neatly sealed and abandoned' and 'people from this region migrated south, east, and west'. The northern outliers at Aztec Ruins go on as the Aztec regional system in Cliopatria (1152-1304); the rest reverts to nobody. 1151 is Cliopatria's last year, the page's round figure is 1150.

certainty.note: Archaeological extents: the page gives a basin area and outlier counts, not frontiers; every edge is approximate.

sources.title: Ancestral Puebloans
sources.note: Golden Age 900-1150, the drought from 1130, the Chacoans abandoning the canyon, descendants merging into the Pueblo peoples; thin on Chaco's extent and silent on a state.

sources.title: Chaco Culture National Historical Park
sources.note: Dates of occupation, great houses and beams (1033-1092), 70 outliers by 1115, the outlier spread (170,000 km2), the San Juan Basin (65,000 km2), the unravelling from about 1140.

notes: Type 'culture' (not 'state'): the pages call Chaco a 'major cultural center' and 'Chacoan culture' and never a state, polity or chiefdom; Cliopatria and Seshat (seed ids us_chaco_1, us_chaco_2) code it as a polity. A state of a kind is not shown by the pages opened, so the renderer should draw it muted. Page budget 1-2: two pages opened (Ancestral Puebloans, Chaco Culture National Historical Park). Wikidata Q478805 is shared with puebloans-aztec-regional-system; the two are kept as two dossiers because Cliopatria and Seshat carry them as separate systems (us_chaco_1/2 versus us_aztec_puebloan), the Chaco shape ends in 1151 with the canyon sealed, and the Aztec shape (8,739 km2) is a northern remnant starting 1152; the pages themselves do not say whether Aztec is a continuation or a successor, and treat both as Ancestral Puebloans, so a reviewer may merge them under this slug with both Names. The Chaco shape of 1040-1151 matches the San Juan Basin area (65,000 km2) given on the page. The Cliopatria 1040 start is not found on the page (it dates a boom 1020-1050 and the beams 1033-1092); the 1151 end is one year past the page's 1150. No ruler list, no wars, no names of counterparts: the pages name no neighbouring state. Regions: Chaco Canyon is searched as 'Pueblo Bonito' (a gazetteer place, -107.96 36.06).
